clusters.name: Your grandfather Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and grew distant from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work and then separated from Celeste; your mother lay awake over them; and your brother Callum developed ear infections through the winter. These shifts pile up from February through May 1979, each touching another person in the family.

clusters.name: Your mother's bed rest in pregnancy, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother ordered to bed for the rest of her pregnancy in March 1984, within those months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house, then argued with your father over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and your sister Ines was born in September. The shifts among these people run from April through June, before the birth settled the household.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis with Parkinson's disease in September 1986, over the following ten years: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments, then gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; your father phoned his father every night for news of her, then argued with Lyle over who should help their parents, then drank most evenings, then fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house; your aunt Pearl developed panic spells at the wheel; and Hazel's functioning fell in steps—a bad fall in 1988, steadier on new medicine in 1988, then decline again through 1991 and 1995. The shifts run close together through the 1980s and into the early 1990s, each person's move touching another's, until Hazel moved to the nursing home in June 1997.

clusters.name: Your brother Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for a job up north in May 1999, within the following year: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father then missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere, even to work; and by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. The shifts among these people run from January 1999 through August 2000, with each person's move near another's.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the following months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night, stopped going to the bookshop and lost your job, dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark, then took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again by November. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
